name: Custom chin implant (silicone/Medpor)

angle.text: Users consider a chin implant to add projection, and sometimes height or width, to a recessed chin, as a less invasive route than sliding genioplasty. The change in profile is visible once healed. Silicone, porous polyethylene and patient-specific designs are discussed, with outcomes documented mainly in surgical case series.

summary: A solid or porous implant placed over the chin bone to add projection: the less invasive alternative to a sliding genioplasty, with its own trade-offs.
note: Implants can shift or be removed later; surgeons and forum users disagree about implant versus bone-moving genioplasty for larger deficiencies.
currentQuick:
A chin implant is a shaped piece of synthetic material, most often silicone or porous polyethylene (Medpor), placed through a cut under the chin or inside the lower lip to push the chin forward. It is a long-established cosmetic operation, often done alongside nose surgery.
In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a cheaper, reversible alternative to sliding genioplasty, with debate over whether it is enough for a very recessed chin and over custom (patient-specific) designs made from CT scans.
How it works: The implant sits on the front of the jawbone and adds bulk, increasing projection and sometimes height or width. Silicone is smooth and removable; porous polyethylene allows tissue ingrowth and is harder to remove. Custom implants are designed from a scan of the individual's jaw.
Risks and caveats: Reported risks include swelling, hematoma, infection, implant displacement, bone changes under the implant, and nerve numbness. Surgical literature notes that complication rates depend on technique and surgeon experience. It is performed as an Rx surgical procedure by licensed surgeons.
deepLead:
A chin implant is an alloplastic (synthetic) device placed over the lower border of the mandible to increase the projection, and sometimes the height or width, of the chin. Common materials are silicone, porous high-density polyethylene (often sold as Medpor), expanded polytetrafluoroethylene and, more recently, patient-specific implants made from materials such as PEEK. 
The operation is commonly performed together with rhinoplasty or a facelift. Surgical reviews describe a continuing debate over whether an implant or an osseous (bone-cutting) genioplasty is the better operation for a given patient, and state that complication avoidance depends on technique and surgeon experience. 
In looksmaxxing communities, chin implants are discussed as a lower-cost, less invasive option than sliding genioplasty, and the term 'custom implant' refers to a design made from the person's own CT scan. A small number of registered trials have compared patient-specific implants with computer-guided genioplasty.

name: Chin filler

angle.text: Chin filler, often called a liquid genioplasty, is used to add projection or length to the chin without surgery, and the change in profile is visible right after treatment. People use it to preview or approximate surgical results. Hyaluronic acid fillers are studied for chin augmentation, with effects that are temporary.

summary: Injectable filler (usually hyaluronic acid) placed at the chin to add projection or length without surgery; temporary, with rare but serious vascular complications.
note: Rare vascular occlusion and tissue necrosis are documented; self-injection by forum users is outside any regulated setting.
currentQuick:
Chin filler is a non-surgical way to add volume to the chin, most often with hyaluronic acid gel injected by a clinician. Companies have run registered trials of several products specifically for chin retrusion, and published case reviews describe its use for reshaping the facial profile.
On looksmax.org it is discussed as a trial run before surgery or a temporary alternative to implants and genioplasty. Forum members also post self-injection accounts, which clinicians regard as outside normal safety conditions.
How it works: Hyaluronic acid or similar gel is injected near the bone to add volume, projecting or lengthening the chin. The effect lasts as long as the material persists in the tissue and is reversible with hyaluronidase for hyaluronic acid products.
Risks and caveats: The chin is generally regarded as a lower-risk injection area, but case reports describe vascular occlusion, skin necrosis and even tongue necrosis after chin filler. Anatomical studies map the arteries to inform safer injection. Fillers are regulated medical devices administered by licensed practitioners.
deepLead:
Chin filler is a non-surgical cosmetic treatment in which an injectable gel, typically hyaluronic acid, is placed in the chin to increase its projection, height or contour. It is sometimes called a liquid genioplasty and is used both for age-related volume loss and for congenital chin retrusion. 
Published work includes a case review of 83 patients treated with combined forehead, nose and chin filler to alter the profile , and manufacturers have registered several trials of specific hyaluronic acid products for chin retrusion.  The literature also documents rare serious complications, including vascular occlusion and tongue necrosis. 
In looksmaxxing communities chin filler is discussed as a reversible, lower-cost alternative or precursor to chin implants and sliding genioplasty. Forum members also post accounts of self-injection; clinical literature on safety concerns the anatomy and complications of professional injection.

name: Vertical chin lengthening

angle.text: Vertical chin lengthening is discussed by people with a short lower third of the face who want a taller chin rather than a more forward one. The height change is visible once healed. The surgical literature on genioplasty with grafts or implants consists mostly of small case series.

summary: Genioplasty (or a graft or implant) that makes the chin taller rather than just more forward; documented in the surgical literature, mostly as small case series.
note: Techniques using grafts carry infection, donor-site and bone-resorption risks described in the literature.
currentQuick:
Vertical chin lengthening is a set of surgical methods that increase the height of the chin, usually by cutting the chin bone and inserting a graft or spacer, or by using an implant. Surgeons describe it for short lower faces, including in East Asian contouring surgery.
The published evidence is largely technique descriptions and case series rather than controlled trials.
How it works: In an osseous genioplasty the chin segment is cut, moved down, and held in place, with a bone graft or other material filling the gap. Variants combine lengthening with narrowing. Alloplastic implants can also add height.
Risks and caveats: The literature mentions infection, donor-site problems and resorption of grafted bone as drawbacks of graft-based methods. It is a surgical procedure performed by licensed surgeons.
deepLead:
Vertical chin lengthening refers to surgical techniques that increase the vertical height of the chin, as distinct from advancing it forward. Methods described in the literature include osseous genioplasty with interpositional bone grafts, pedicled grafts, and alloplastic materials. 
Authors describe the operation for patients with a short lower face or a short and wide lower face, particularly in East Asian aesthetic surgery, where it may be combined with narrowing of the chin.  A report from 1987 discusses lengthening and shortening of the chin by adding or removing bone and states that results improved with miniplate fixation. 
No randomized trials of vertical chin lengthening were found; the evidence consists of technique papers and retrospective series.

name: Chin reduction / shaving

angle.text: Chin reduction is discussed by people whose chin looks too large or prominent and who want a smaller, better-proportioned lower face. The reduction in size is visible once healed. Techniques include burring the bone and osteotomy with setback, described in surgical papers.

summary: Surgery to shrink a large chin by burring the bone or moving it back and up; documented in surgical papers, with nerve and contour risks.
note: Surgeons list mental nerve injury, bony irregularity and chin pad ptosis as potential sequelae.
currentQuick:
Chin reduction is surgery to make a long, protruding or wide chin smaller. The two classical approaches are an osteotomy that moves the chin bone back or up, and burring (shaving) the surface of the bone.
The published evidence is made up of technique descriptions and case series, including work on setback with reduction genioplasty for long chins and on feminization surgery.
How it works: A segment of chin bone can be cut and repositioned (reduction or setback genioplasty), or prominent bone can be burred down. Another described approach removes bone and soft tissue from under the chin.
Risks and caveats: Surgical papers state that both main approaches have potential negative aesthetic sequelae, including mental nerve injury, bony contour irregularities, increased submental soft-tissue fullness and chin pad ptosis. It is performed under anaesthetic by licensed surgeons.
deepLead:
Chin reduction refers to surgical procedures that reduce the size of the chin in projection, height or width. A 1999 paper states that, at that time, surgical reduction of an isolated large chin was not a simple procedure, and that two operations existed: osteotomy with setback, or reduction of the prominence by burring. 
Reduction genioplasty is also used together with mandibular setback for prognathism and a long chin , and a box-shaped chin impaction osteotomy has been reported as part of mandibular feminization surgery. 
No trials comparing chin-reduction techniques were found; the literature consists of technique papers and case series.

name: Double-jaw surgery for retrognathia

angle.text: Double-jaw surgery is the major structural option discussed for a recessed lower jaw, moving the mandible and upper jaw forward together to improve both bite and profile. The skeletal change is visible and measurable after healing. It is a well-established orthognathic operation with an extensive surgical literature.

summary: Bimaxillary (upper and lower jaw) surgery that moves a recessed mandible forward, often with the maxilla and chin; a major established operation with documented joint and nerve risks.
note: Major surgery: reported complications include nerve injury, infection and condylar changes; forum users debate single-jaw versus double-jaw plans.
currentQuick:
Double-jaw (bimaxillary) surgery repositions both the upper and lower jaw, usually after orthodontic preparation, to correct a recessed lower jaw (retrognathia), bite problems and facial proportions. It is a long-established operation in oral and maxillofacial surgery, and sometimes is combined with a genioplasty.
In looksmaxxing communities it sits at the top of the 'hardmaxxing' ladder, and members discuss whether a single-jaw plan can do the job.
How it works: Surgeons cut the jaws (typically a bilateral sagittal split osteotomy of the mandible and a Le Fort I osteotomy of the maxilla), move them to a planned position, and fix them with plates and screws. Planning uses imaging and often 3D software.
Risks and caveats: Reported risks include temporary or permanent numbness from nerve injury, infection, bleeding and swelling, and in some patients condylar atrophy or joint changes after bimaxillary surgery. Recovery is typically measured in weeks to months.
deepLead:
Double-jaw surgery, or bimaxillary surgery, is an orthognathic operation in which both the maxilla (upper jaw) and the mandible (lower jaw) are cut, repositioned and fixed. For retrognathia, a recessed lower jaw, the mandible is advanced, commonly through a bilateral sagittal split osteotomy, and the upper jaw is moved to match the bite. 
Orthognathic surgery is described as corrective jaw surgery usually done through the mouth, in coordination with an orthodontist. Encyclopedic accounts trace its development from a case published in 1849 through the mid-twentieth-century popularisation of the sagittal split by Hugo Obwegeser.  A 1957 paper on correction of mandibular prognathism and retrognathia considered genioplasty as part of surgical reshaping of the chin. 
In looksmaxxing forums, double-jaw surgery is discussed as a major hardmaxxing option, with threads comparing it with single-jaw surgery plus genioplasty.

name: Profile analysis (Ricketts E-line)

chain: Line drawn nose tip to chin
Profile goals for chin and lips
angle.text: Forum users apply the E-line to side-profile photos to judge where the lips sit relative to the nose and chin, and to decide whether chin or lip changes are of interest. It is a standard orthodontic reference measurement. Preferred lip positions vary between observers and over time.

summary: A line from nose tip to chin used to judge how far the lips sit from the profile; a standard orthodontic reference, with preferences that vary by observer.
note: Norms are population averages; studies show esthetic preferences differ across observer groups.
currentQuick:
The Ricketts esthetic line, or E-line, is drawn from the tip of the soft-tissue nose to the soft-tissue chin (pogonion) on a side-view image. Orthodontists use the distance from the lips to this line to describe how full or retrusive the profile is.
It is one of several profile analyses, and looksmaxxing discussions of chin and lip position borrow it as a way to describe the relationship between nose, lips and chin.
How it works: On a lateral cephalogram or profile photograph the line is drawn and the lower lip is measured against it. Wikipedia lists a published mean for lower lip to E-line of minus 2 mm with a standard deviation of 2 mm.
Risks and caveats: This is a measurement convention rather than a treatment. Cephalometric measurements are two-dimensional, and studies show that preferred profiles differ among observers of different backgrounds.
deepLead:
The E-line, or esthetic plane, is a soft-tissue reference line defined in Ricketts cephalometric analysis as running from the tip of the soft-tissue nose to the soft-tissue pogonion. It is used to describe the position of the lips relative to the nose and chin, with the lower lip to E-line distance (Li-EL) as a standard measurement. 
Orthodontic and surgical planning use it, and studies of profile change after orthodontic treatment have measured lip position relative to esthetic lines.  Research has also compared skeletofacial morphology of faces judged attractive and not attractive, and studies show that esthetic preferences for lip position differ among observer groups. 
In looksmaxxing culture the line is used informally for discussing chin and lip balance; the sources reviewed contain little direct community discussion of it.

name: Orthodontic functional appliances (Herbst, Twin Block)

chain: Lower jaw grows or shifts forward
angle.text: Users interested in profile improvement discuss Herbst and Twin Block appliances for growing teens with a recessed lower jaw and overbite. They are studied in randomized trials in adolescents, where how much change is jaw growth versus tooth movement is debated. Use in adults for facial appearance rests on anecdote.

summary: Orthodontist-fitted jaw-advancing braces for growing teens with an overbite; studied in randomized trials, but how much is real jaw growth versus tooth movement is debated.
note: Designed for growing patients; skeletal change in adults is limited without surgery.
currentQuick:
Functional appliances such as the Herbst and Twin Block are orthodontic devices that hold the lower jaw forward in children and teens with a Class II bite, where the lower jaw sits behind the upper. They are prescribed and fitted by orthodontists, usually before or around the pubertal growth spurt.
On looksmaxxing forums they are discussed as a way to correct a 'recessed' jaw or overbite while still growing, with users asking about cost, adult use, and cheaper substitutes.
How it works: The Herbst uses telescoping rods fixed to the teeth to keep the jaw forward; the Twin Block uses removable interlocking bite plates. Research distinguishes small amounts of extra mandibular growth and upper-jaw restraint from movement of the teeth themselves.
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include initial discomfort, chewing and speech difficulty, spacing between teeth, and possible gum or root effects with heavy tooth movement. Benefits in adults are limited, and over-the-counter substitutes have not been studied for this purpose.
deepLead:
Orthodontic functional appliances are devices that hold or guide the lower jaw forward in growing children and adolescents, mainly to treat Class II malocclusion, in which the lower jaw sits behind the upper one and the upper front teeth overlap the lower ones. The best-known examples are the Herbst appliance, a fixed device with telescoping arms bonded to the teeth, and the Twin Block, a removable pair of acrylic bite plates .
The Herbst appliance was developed by the German orthodontist Emil Herbst in the early 1900s and reintroduced in modern form by Hans Pancherz in 1979 . Because it is fixed, it does not depend on the patient remembering to wear it, and treatment typically runs for several months . The Twin Block was studied in a multicentre randomized trial in the United Kingdom in children aged 8 to 10 .
Published research, including a systematic review, has examined how much of the correction comes from extra lower-jaw growth versus tooth movement . Within looksmaxxing communities, the devices are discussed as a way to advance a 'recessed' jaw during the teenage years, and some users ask whether adults or home-made alternatives can achieve similar changes .

name: Neck posture / forward head correction

chain: Chin and neck line up better
angle.text: Forum posters promote correcting forward head posture to sharpen the jawline and profile, since the head sits further over the shoulders when upright. Posture correction is well studied for neck pain, but its effect on how the chin and jaw look has not been tested.

summary: Pulling the head back over the shoulders to sharpen the profile; heavily studied for neck pain, but nobody has tested whether it changes how the chin looks.
note: Forums disagree on whether correction helps or hurts chin appearance; no appearance studies exist.
currentQuick:
Forward head posture is when the head sits ahead of the shoulders. It is common with heavy screen use and is usually measured with the craniovertebral angle.
Research links it mainly to neck pain and headache. On looksmaxxing forums, people debate whether fixing it improves the jawline and profile or makes a weak chin look worse.
How it works: Correction usually means postural habits, ergonomic changes and neck or upper-back exercises. Proponents say a better head position improves the visual line from chin to neck; no study has tested this.
Risks and caveats: Posture exercises are generally low risk and studied in the context of neck pain. The appearance claims are untested, and some forum users report that a chin tuck can make a recessed chin look less prominent.
deepLead:
Forward head posture (FHP), sometimes called 'text neck' or 'nerd neck', is a posture in which the head sits forward of the shoulders, so the ear falls in front of a vertical line through the shoulder and the chin appears to poke forward . It is usually assessed clinically with the craniovertebral angle, formed between a horizontal line at the seventh cervical vertebra and a line to the ear .
Most published research on forward head posture concerns neck pain, headache and disability rather than appearance . A 2019 systematic review and meta-analysis examined the relationship between forward head posture and neck pain . Wikipedia reports that this meta-analysis found a correlation in adults but not in adolescents .
In looksmaxxing communities, head posture is discussed as something that changes how the chin, jawline and profile look, and the claims run in both directions: some say correcting posture improves the profile, others say it makes a recessed chin look worse . No published study located for this article has tested whether posture correction changes facial appearance.

name: Jaw advancement for sleep apnea (MAD devices)

angle.text: Mandibular advancement devices are a sleep-apnea mouthpiece, and some forum users wonder whether wearing one could also shift the lower jaw forward for a better profile. They are well studied for snoring and breathing during sleep, while any facial-appearance effect is untested.

summary: A sleep-apnea mouthpiece that pushes the lower jaw forward; well studied for breathing, with no evidence it changes your face.
note: Medical device for sleep apnea; long-term use is associated with changes in how the teeth meet.
currentQuick:
Mandibular advancement devices are mouthpieces worn at night that hold the lower jaw forward to keep the airway open. They are prescribed for snoring and obstructive sleep apnea, often when CPAP is not tolerated.
They are connected to looksmaxxing mainly through interest in jaw position and airway; no study has tested them for changing facial appearance.
How it works: Holding the jaw forward tightens upper-airway tissues and reduces collapse and vibration during sleep. The effect lasts only while the device is worn.
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include dry mouth, tooth and jaw pain, and long-term changes in how the teeth meet. Many users stop because of discomfort. Cheap non-prescription versions are unproven, and some specialists consider them potentially dangerous.
deepLead:
A mandibular advancement device (MAD), also called a mandibular advancement splint or oral appliance, is a mouthpiece worn during sleep that holds the lower jaw slightly forward. It is used to treat snoring and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), a condition of repeated airway collapse during sleep .
The devices are medical products rather than facial-aesthetics tools. Wikipedia reports that the American Academy of Sleep Medicine and the American Academy of Dental Sleep Medicine recommend oral appliances for primary snoring and for people with OSA who cannot tolerate CPAP or prefer another therapy . Randomized trials have compared MADs with continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) .
The topic appears in looksmaxxing contexts because the same forward jaw position is associated with jaw and airway discussions, and because some people ask whether such devices can change facial structure. No published trial has tested MADs as an appearance treatment.

name: Fat grafting to chin

angle.text: Fat grafting is discussed as a way to build out a small chin using the person's own fat, as an alternative to implants, genioplasty or fillers. The added volume is visible after treatment. Fat grafting is an established technique in general, with limited chin-specific data, and some of the fat can be reabsorbed.

summary: Using your own fat to build out the chin; a recognized surgical technique in general, but the sources show little chin-specific evidence and the fat can partly resorb.
note: Grafted fat can be partly reabsorbed and changes with weight; no chin-specific data in the sources reviewed.
currentQuick:
Fat grafting takes fat from elsewhere on the body, processes it and injects it into an area to add volume. For the chin, it is an alternative to implants or fillers for adding projection or fullness.
The sources reviewed give general information on fat transfer but no chin-specific outcome data.
How it works: Fat is harvested, prepared and reinjected. Part of it survives as living tissue and part may be reabsorbed, and the result can change with weight gain or loss.
Risks and caveats: Reported general risks include fat necrosis, swelling, bruising, asymmetry or lumpiness, infection and donor-site pain. It is a surgical procedure performed by clinicians.
deepLead:
Fat grafting, also called fat transfer or lipofilling, moves a person's own fat from one body area to another. It involves harvesting fat, processing it and reinjecting it, and is used to add volume or smooth irregular areas . Applied to the chin, it is one of several ways to change chin projection or contour, alongside implants, sliding genioplasty and injectable fillers .
Wikipedia reports that transferred fat can be partly reabsorbed, with up to 50% resorption cited for breast augmentation, and that weight gain or loss can affect results because grafted fat behaves like fat elsewhere in the body . The pages reviewed for this entry do not give outcome data specific to the chin.

name: Weight loss for chin definition

angle.text: Users lose body fat to reduce submental fullness and show the chin and jawline more clearly, mainly where a double chin is soft tissue. It changes the covering fat rather than bone structure. No studies test fat loss specifically for chin definition.

summary: Losing body fat to reveal the chin and jawline; plausible where fullness is soft tissue, but no studies test it and bone structure is not changed.
note: Wikipedia notes a double-chin look can also come from bone structure, not fat.
currentQuick:
Weight loss for chin definition is the idea that lowering overall body fat reduces fullness under the chin and makes the jawline look sharper.
Wikipedia describes a double chin as arising either from soft-tissue fat or from jaw bones that do not project far enough; no study found here tests weight loss for chin appearance.
How it works: Reducing overall body fat shrinks fat cells, including those under the chin. The sources reviewed do not address whether fat loss can be targeted to one area.
Risks and caveats: The sources reviewed list no risks specific to this approach. When the cause is bone structure, fat loss is not described as changing the chin's projection.
deepLead:
Weight loss for chin definition refers to the idea that reducing body fat makes the chin and jawline look sharper by reducing fullness under the chin, often called a double chin. Wikipedia distinguishes two causes of a double-chin appearance: in some overweight people, subcutaneous fat around the neck creates a fold, while in others, often of normal weight, the jaw bones do not project far enough forward .
Wikipedia describes surgical fat removal for the first type and jaw or chin surgery for the bony type, but it gives no outcome data for either . The pages reviewed do not address whether fat can be lost from the chin area selectively, and no study located for this entry tests weight loss as a way to change chin appearance.

name: Submalar filler

angle.text: Submalar filler is used to add volume in the hollow beneath the cheekbone, as a non-surgical counterpart to submalar implants. The change in cheek contour is visible after treatment and is temporary. Evidence in the sources reviewed consists of small registered trials.

summary: Filler injected below the cheekbone to add lower-midface volume; temporary, with only small registered trials in the sources reviewed.
note: Fillers are eventually resorbed; asymmetry is a listed risk.
currentQuick:
Submalar filler adds volume to the hollow beneath the cheekbones, aiming for a more defined or fuller lower midface. It is injected by clinicians, typically using hyaluronic acid.
The sources reviewed contain general cheek-augmentation information and small registered trials, but little outcome data specific to this area.
How it works: A gel filler is injected into the tissue below the cheekbone, adding volume until the body gradually resorbs it.
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia lists asymmetry from uneven resorption or shifting among risks of cheek augmentation. Filler is eventually resorbed, so results are temporary.
deepLead:
Submalar filler is an injectable filler placed in the hollow below the cheekbone to add volume to the lower midface. It is a non-surgical counterpart to submalar implants, which Wikipedia describes as augmenting the midface, while malar implants sit on the cheekbones .
Wikipedia names hyaluronic acid products such as Restylane and Juvederm and autologous fat as materials used for cheek augmentation, and notes that fillers are eventually resorbed . Registered clinical trials have tested hyaluronic acid and other fillers for midface volume and cheek augmentation .

name: Malar augmentation with fat grafting

angle.text: People use fat grafting to add volume and projection over the cheekbones with their own tissue, as an alternative to implants or hyaluronic acid fillers. The added fullness is visible after treatment. Fat grafting is widely used in the face, though cheek-specific evidence is thin and some fat can be reabsorbed.

summary: Your own liposuctioned fat injected into the cheeks for volume; plausible and widely used in the face, but cheek-specific evidence is thin.
note: Some grafted fat is resorbed, so results can vary.
currentQuick:
Malar fat grafting uses fat taken from elsewhere on the body, processed and injected into the cheeks to add fullness and projection.
It is discussed as a natural-tissue alternative to implants or fillers. Evidence specific to cheek augmentation is limited in the sources reviewed.
How it works: Fat is harvested by liposuction, purified and reinjected into the cheek area; the portion that survives provides lasting volume, and the rest is resorbed.
Risks and caveats: Reported risks of fat grafting include swelling, bruising, infection, lumpiness or contour irregularity, fat necrosis and unpredictable resorption. It is a medical procedure performed by surgeons.
deepLead:
Malar augmentation with fat grafting is a cosmetic procedure in which a person's own fat is harvested, usually by liposuction from another body site, processed, and injected into the cheek area to add volume and projection over the cheekbones. It is a form of autologous (self-derived) soft-tissue augmentation, distinct from cheek implants and from hyaluronic acid fillers.
In appearance-focused communities it is discussed as a softer-tissue alternative to implants for fuller or more defined cheeks. General fat-grafting sources describe facial uses as restoring volume to deflated facial compartments, and note that some transferred fat is resorbed over time, so outcomes can vary.
Published evidence specific to cheek augmentation is not included in the sources compiled here. The one registered trial linked to this entry studied fat grafting for acne scars, not cheek contour.

name: Zygomatic arch reduction / reduction malarplasty

angle.text: Reduction malarplasty is used to narrow wide or prominent cheekbones, and is among the more commonly requested facial-contour procedures in East Asia. The narrower face is visible after healing. Support comes mainly from surgeon case series.

summary: Cheekbone-narrowing osteotomy, mainly an East Asian aesthetic surgery, supported only by surgeon case series.
note: Major bone surgery with nerve injury and nonunion reported.
currentQuick:
Reduction malarplasty cuts and repositions the cheekbone to narrow a wide or prominent midface. Surgeons describe it as a commonly requested contouring procedure in East Asia.
The published literature is mostly retrospective case series and technique papers.
How it works: Osteotomies are made in the malar complex or zygomatic arch, through coronal, intraoral, preauricular or small percutaneous incisions, and the bone is repositioned or fixed.
Risks and caveats: Reported concerns include scars and facial-nerve injury with some approaches, and zygomatic nonunion after surgery. It is major surgery performed by trained surgeons.
deepLead:
Reduction malarplasty is a facial-bone surgery that narrows a wide or prominent cheekbone (zygoma) by cutting and repositioning the malar complex or zygomatic arch. Published authors describe it as one of the more commonly requested facial-contour procedures in East Asia and as rarely performed in the West.
Techniques have evolved from coronal-incision approaches, which leave a scalp scar and carry facial-nerve risk, toward intraoral and limited-incision osteotomies. The literature is made up of surgeon case series and technique descriptions; randomized trials were not found.
In looksmaxxing forums the term ZSO (zygomatic skeletal osteotomy) appears mostly in discussions about the opposite aim, projecting or repositioning cheekbones, and posters often compare it with malar implants and midface advancement.

name: Cheekbone makeup contour/highlight

angle.text: Users apply darker shades beneath the cheekbone and lighter or shimmering shades on top to make cheekbones look more defined for photos or an evening. The effect is visible immediately and washes off. It is a cosmetic technique with no clinical research behind it.

summary: Shading and highlighting to imitate defined cheekbones; reversible and low-risk, with no clinical research behind it.
note: Effect is visual and depends on lighting and application.
currentQuick:
Cheekbone contouring uses darker and lighter makeup to suggest more defined cheekbones.
It is a styling technique and has not been studied clinically.
How it works: Shading under the cheekbone and highlighting on top change the perceived depth and shape of the cheek through light and shadow.
Risks and caveats: Makeup carries the usual risks of skin irritation or allergic reaction with some products. The effect is temporary and washes off.
deepLead:
Cheekbone contouring and highlighting is a makeup technique in which darker shades are applied beneath the cheekbone and lighter or shimmering shades on top, intended to create the visual impression of more defined or higher cheekbones through shading.
The technique is discussed in style-focused parts of appearance communities as a non-surgical, reversible way to change perceived facial structure. No clinical studies on the effect were found, and the technique is a cosmetic styling practice rather than a medical treatment.

name: Midface lift

chain: Fuller cheek, less hollow lower lid
angle.text: A midface lift repositions sagging cheek and lower-eyelid tissue upward to restore a fuller, younger cheek and soften a hollowed lower lid. The lift is visible once healed. It is described as suited to people in their 40s without marked jowling, with evidence mostly from surgeon case series.

summary: Surgery that lifts sagging cheek tissue; established in facial plastic surgery but backed mostly by surgeon case series.
note: Surgical risks include lid malposition and dry eye reported around related procedures.
currentQuick:
A midface lift raises cheek and lower-eyelid tissue to restore volume and reduce hollowing. It is often discussed for people in their 40s and is frequently combined with eyelid surgery.
Evidence comes mainly from surgeon case series and technique reviews.
How it works: Surgeons elevate and resuspend midface soft tissue, via approaches such as the malar fat pad or high SMAS flap, through incisions near the hairline, eyelid or mouth.
Risks and caveats: Reported complications in related eyelid and facelift surgery include lid malposition and dry-eye symptoms. It is major surgery performed by trained surgeons.
deepLead:
A midface lift is a cosmetic surgical procedure that repositions sagging cheek and lower-eyelid tissue upward, aiming to restore a fuller, younger-looking cheek and reduce the appearance of a hollowed lower lid. It is typically described as suited to patients in their 40s without marked jowling, and it can be combined with eyelid surgery.
Techniques have changed over decades, from approaches such as elevating the malar fat pad to high-SMAS facelift designs that extend the dissection to mobilize midface tissue. Published evidence consists mainly of surgeon case series and technique reviews.
Within looksmaxxing discussions it appears in the context of combined facial-implant and rhinoplasty results shared by patients.

name: Maxilla expansion for forward growth (face pulling/reverse-pull headgear)

angle.text: Forum users discuss reverse-pull headgear, or face pulling, as a way to bring the upper jaw and midface forward for a better profile. It is studied in children with underbites and a retrusive maxilla. Its use as an appearance tool in adults is based on anecdote.

summary: Orthodontic facemask that pulls a child's upper jaw forward; studied in kids with underbites, not an adult appearance tool.
note: Evidence applies to growing children; some relapse reported.
currentQuick:
Reverse-pull headgear is an orthodontic device used in children with underbites and a recessed upper jaw to pull the maxilla forward.
Studies in children report forward skeletal change, though some patients relapse in the long term.
How it works: Elastics from the teeth to a frame on the forehead and chin apply forward force, often after rapid palatal expansion, to remodel the sutures around the maxilla.
Risks and caveats: Dentoalveolar side effects and relapse are reported. Use is guided by an orthodontist, and the evidence concerns growing children.
deepLead:
Reverse-pull headgear, also called a facemask or protraction facemask, is an orthodontic appliance with a frame in front of the face resting on the forehead and chin, with elastics attached to the teeth to pull the upper jaw forward. It is used in children with Class III malocclusion and a retrusive maxilla, often together with rapid palatal expansion.
Orthodontic literature reports that treatment in the deciduous and mixed dentition can produce skeletal forward movement of the maxilla through remodeling of the circummaxillary sutures, though it is often accompanied by dentoalveolar effects. Long-term follow-up shows that some patients relapse.
In appearance communities the entry is discussed as a way to move the midface forward, and the evidence concerns growing children, not adults.

name: Facial thread lift (cheek lifting)

angle.text: Thread lifts are used as a minimally invasive way to raise the midface and soften the nasolabial fold without removing skin. The lift is visible after the procedure. Efficacy data are limited and mixed, with complications reported in the literature.

summary: Threads placed under the skin to hoist the cheeks; minimally invasive, with unclear efficacy data and reported complications.
note: Practitioner training and complications have drawn media scrutiny.
currentQuick:
A thread lift uses threads inserted under the skin to lift the cheeks and midface without cutting away skin.
Trials are registered, but published outcome data were not available in the sources reviewed.
How it works: Threads, some barbed or coated, anchor and elevate tissue, and are placed through small entry points.
Risks and caveats: Physician and media reports describe infection, vessel puncture and pain, and some threads cannot easily be removed. Practitioner qualifications vary by country.
deepLead:
A thread lift is a non-surgical or minimally invasive procedure in which threads, some with barbs or cones, are placed under the skin to lift facial tissue without removing skin. Applied to the cheeks, it is used to raise the midface and soften the nasolabial fold.
Wikipedia describes it as a simplified alternative to a facelift and reports physician and media concerns about complications and about training standards. Two registered trials exist, one comparing hyaluronic acid-coated and non-coated threads for the midface and one combining threads with microfocused ultrasound. Results were not available in the sources reviewed.

name: Cheek fat pad (Bichat) removal

angle.text: Buccal fat removal is popular in looksmaxxing communities as a route to hollow cheeks and a more visible cheekbone-to-jaw transition, often tied to the ogee curve. The slimmer lower cheek is visible after healing. Published outcome data are limited.

summary: Surgical removal of the cheek fat pad for slimmer, hollower cheeks; popular online, with little published outcome data and nerve and duct risks.
note: Wikipedia notes risk of facial nerve branch and parotid duct injury; DIY attempts are reported in forums.
currentQuick:
Cheek fat pad removal takes out part of the buccal fat pad in the cheek, usually through an incision inside the mouth, to slim the lower face. Forum users link it to hollow cheeks and the ogee curve.
The pad is well documented as a surgical flap in mouth and sinus surgery, but published outcome data for purely cosmetic removal are limited in the sources reviewed.
How it works: The buccal fat pad sits deep in the cheek under the masseter and zygomaticus muscles. Removing some of its volume reduces fullness in the lower cheek, which proponents say reveals cheekbone and jaw structure.
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia reports a significant risk of injury to the buccal branch of the facial nerve and the parotid duct. Self-performed removal has been described on forums, and other members in those threads warn against it.
deepLead:
Cheek fat pad (Bichat) removal, also called buccal fat removal or bichectomy, is a surgical procedure in which part or all of the buccal fat pad, an encapsulated mass of fat deep in the cheek, is taken out, usually through the mouth, to reduce fullness of the lower cheek . In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a route to hollow cheeks and a more visible cheekbone-to-jaw transition, often alongside the idea of the ogee curve.
The buccal fat pad lies between the buccinator muscle and the more superficial masseter and zygomaticus muscles, and it contributes to cheek hollowing and the nasolabial fold . Surgical literature has mainly studied the pad as a pedicled flap for closing defects between the mouth and maxillary sinus , and for its regenerative cells . A registered trial of an intraoral removal technique has been completed, but its results are not listed among the sources reviewed here .
Wikipedia notes that removal may carry a significant risk of injury to the buccal branch of the facial nerve and the parotid duct . Imaging reviews of cosmetic facial procedures also discuss how fat removal and fat-pad changes appear after surgery . Looksmax.org users have also posted accounts of attempted do-it-yourself removal; these are not documented in the research literature and are not described here.

name: Hollow cheeks via chewing then fat loss

angle.text: Forum posters combine masseter-focused chewing with fat loss to bring out cheekbones and jaw structure and create hollow cheeks. They describe hollowness as coming from bone and muscle, revealed by less soft tissue. No studies test the combination.

summary: Chew for the masseter, lean out for the cheeks; popular in forums, but no studies test the combination.
note: No trial found for chewing plus fat loss; medical literature on hollow cheeks concerns volume restoration.
currentQuick:
This approach pairs chewing exercises aimed at the masseter with weight and facial fat loss, in the hope of showing cheekbones and a hollow below them.
Forum members disagree about the look itself, and no clinical study of the combination was found.
How it works: Believers say hollows come from cheekbone projection, jaw angle and masseter size, which become visible when facial fat is low. Wikipedia notes the buccal fat pad also contributes to cheek fullness.
Risks and caveats: No harms were documented for the combination in the sources reviewed. Medical literature associates very hollow cheeks with aging or lipodystrophy, conditions treated with volume restoration.
deepLead:
"Hollow cheeks via chewing then fat loss" refers to a looksmaxxing approach that combines masseter-focused chewing with reducing body and facial fat, in order to show cheekbone and jaw structure. Proponents describe hollow cheeks as the shadowed area below the cheekbones, produced by bone, muscle and the amount of soft tissue .
No published trial was found that tests chewing followed by fat loss for cheek hollowing. Medical literature in this area concerns facial fat loss from aging and lipodystrophy, and treatments such as fillers and fat grafting to restore cheek volume . Wikipedia notes the buccal fat pad contributes to cheek hollowing, but it describes no chewing-based method .
